title: trainDictionary
body:
## trainDictionary

Learn a reusable, explicitly identified compression dictionary from a captured corpus of related small files.

Native binding: `zstd --train-fastcover / --train-cover / --train-legacy --maxdict --dictID`. Output kind: `["file","text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `samples` | List related small files from the population you intend to compress. Keep different records for held-out evaluation; a dictionary trained on the test record gives misleading size gains. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096},"minItems":8,"maxItems":128}` | **required** |
| `algorithm` | FastCover prioritises training speed; Cover searches segment coverage directly; legacy selects older dictionary construction. Only controls relevant to the chosen algorithm may be authored. | `{"type":"enum","values":["fastCover","cover","legacy"]}` | `"fastCover"` |
| `maxDictionaryBytes` | Maximum trained dictionary length in bytes. Choose a small reusable dictionary appropriate to the typical record size and provide a substantially larger representative sample corpus. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":256,"maximum":1048576}` | `16384` |
| `id` | For dictionary training this is the positive public numeric dictionary ID. Inside a comparison profile this is its distinct readable result name. Neither form is a signature. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":4294967295}` | `32768` |
| `segmentSize` | Cover segment length k in bytes; zero selects native automatic search. An explicit value requires dmerSize and must be at least that d-mer length. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":2048}` | `0` |
| `dmerSize` | Length d of short sequences used to estimate corpus coverage. Zero chooses automatic search. FastCover accepts only 6 or 8 explicitly; Cover permits its wider declared range. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":16}` | `0` |
| `steps` | Number of segment-length candidates considered by automatic Cover or FastCover search. More candidates increase training time; this has no effect on the number of output dictionary records. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":64}` | `4` |
| `frequencyLog` | Base-two logarithm of the FastCover frequency table entry count. Larger tables use more memory and reduce hash collisions. This control is refused for other algorithms. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":10,"maximum":23}` | `20` |
| `acceleration` | Higher values sample more sparsely during training to reduce time, potentially worsening dictionary quality. This is independent of compression fast-mode acceleration. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":10}` | `1` |
| `trainingFraction` | Fraction of captured samples used for training, with the remainder used for native selection. Specify whole-percent precision and retain at least five training samples. The adaptor translates the fraction into the CLI integer percentage. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0.1,"maximum":1}` | `0.75` |
| `shrink` | Allow Cover to reduce dictionary size when its held-out compression result is sufficiently close. FastCover and legacy refuse this control. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
| `shrinkRegression` | Cover dictionary shrinking may trade this percentage of compression performance for a smaller dictionary. Requires Cover shrink mode; it does not apply to FastCover or legacy training. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":100}` | `1` |
| `selectivity` | Legacy training selectivity parameter s. It is not a Cover search-step count and is refused for both Cover algorithms. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":20}` | `9` |
| `trainingLevel` | Compression level 1–19 used by native dictionary training to evaluate candidate dictionaries. This does not force later users of the dictionary to use that same level. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":19}` | `3` |
| `sampleBlockBytes` | Zero treats each selected file as a record. A positive value of at least 64 bytes splits the sample corpus into training blocks, useful when records are stored in large files. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":1048576}` | `0` |
